params.body:
Two design notes on how the owner's agents get work done without approval paralysis. These are notes only; nothing here changes code.

**`docs/mandates.md`, "Commands, modelled on blast radius"**

An agent uses commands rather than screens. Each command has a name, typed parameters, the system's own business logic behind it, and a blast radius that decides the approval:

| Layer | Approval |
|---|---|
| B1 | 30-day mandate |
| B2 | per day |
| B3 | per action |
| B4 | after a dry run |
| B5 | never mandated |

Rules for keeping a command's radius low:

- narrow scope;
- a dry run by default;
- reversible where it can be;
- reading kept apart from writing;
- through the app's own logic rather than raw SQL;
- personal data as a command of its own;
- no outbound channel in a run that read customer data.

The note catalogues both systems from an inventory of what they offer today:

- **Stocklist:** insights, measures, stock and checks as B1; photo repair and module switch as B2; resends and transport price as B3. A list names what is never mandated.
- **The Gentells pipeline:** status, mix, cost and the Observatory tools as B1, now built; retry, cron, stop, run and the undo-backed edits as B2; a patch without undo as B3.

**`docs/working-set.md`, new**

- The owner signs a working set once on the YubiKey: projects, the highest layer, and an end date.
- Inside it, every approval is a passkey touch, wherever he is; outside it, the YubiKey again. A compromised Portal can do at most what the set allows, and the chain ends at a person's key.
- The gateway reads a signed, forward-only policy log every minute instead of being carried a configuration and rebooted. A narrowing applies itself, and every record names the policy version it was judged under. The documents are served through Portal; their hashes are public and anchored.
- Four questions stay open: the strong key over NFC from the phone, the longest a set may stand, B3 inside a set, and revocation.
